drivingQuestion: Do the dead know what happens in the world of the living — their own pain only, or the affairs of others too?
outcomeNote: Each of the three תא שמע proofs that the dead know is deflected (איניש אחרינא, the angel Duma, Shmuel's eminence), yet R' Yonatan's reported retraction and his derasha on ״לאמר״ are left standing, and the unit closes on the appended teachings about disparaging the dead and Torah scholars rather than on a decision.

segments.he: בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא נְפוּק לְקִרְיָיתָא. אִייַּקַּר לְהוּ תַּלְמוּדַיְיהוּ. הֲווֹ קָא מִצַּעֲרִי לְאִדְּכוֹרֵיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ חַד לְחַבְרֵיהּ: יָדַע אֲבוּן בְּהַאי צַעֲרָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ אִידַּךְ: מְנָא יָדַע? וְהָא כְּתִיב: ״יִכְבְּדוּ בָנָיו וְלֹא יֵדָע״.
segments.en: The Gemara relates a story on this topic: «The sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya went out to the villages» to oversee the laborers. «They forgot what they had learned and were struggling to recall it. One» of them «said to the other:» Does «our» deceased «father know of» our «anguish? The other said to him: From where would he know? Isn’t it written: “His sons are honored yet he shall not know it,» they come to sorrow and he shall not understand them” (Job 14:21)? The dead do not know.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אִידַּךְ: וְלָא יָדַע? וְהָא כְּתִיב: ״אַךְ בְּשָׂרוֹ עָלָיו יִכְאָב וְנַפְשׁוֹ עָלָיו תֶּאֱבָל״. וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: קָשָׁה רִמָּה לַמֵּת כְּמַחַט בַּבָּשָׂר הַחַי!
segments.en: «The other said» back «to him: And» do the dead truly «not know? Isn’t it written: “Only in his flesh does he feel pain, in his soul does he mourn”» (Job 14:22)? Based on this verse «Rabbi Yitzḥak said:» Gnawing «maggots are as excruciating to the dead as» the stab of «a needle to the flesh of the living.» The dead must have the capacity to feel and know.

segments.he: אָמְרִי: בְּצַעֲרָא דִידְהוּ — יָדְעִי, בְּצַעֲרָא דְאַחֲרִינָא — לָא יָדְעִי.
segments.en: In order to reconcile this contradiction «they said:» They «know of their own pain but do not know of the pain of others.»

segments.he: וְלָא? וְהָתַנְיָא: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּחָסִיד אֶחָד שֶׁנָּתַן דִּינָר לְעָנִי בְּעֶרֶב רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בִּשְׁנֵי בַצּוֹרֶת, וְהִקְנִיטַתּוּ אִשְׁתּוֹ, וְהָלַךְ וְלָן בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת. וְשָׁמַע שְׁתֵּי רוּחוֹת שֶׁמְסַפְּרוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ. אָמְרָה חֲדָא לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ: חֲבֶרְתִּי, בּוֹאִי וְנָשׁוּט בָּעוֹלָם, וְנִשְׁמַע מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַפַּרְגּוֹד מַה פּוּרְעָנוּת בָּא לָעוֹלָם? אָמְרָה לָהּ חֲבֶרְתָּהּ: אֵינִי יְכוֹלָה, שֶׁאֲנִי קְבוּרָה בְּמַחְצֶלֶת שֶׁל קָנִים. אֶלָּא לְכִי אַתְּ, וּמַה שֶּׁאַתְּ שׁוֹמַעַת אִמְרִי לִי. הָלְכָה הִיא וְשָׁטָה וּבָאָה. וְאָמְרָה לָהּ חֲבֶרְתָּהּ: חֲבֶרְתִּי, מַה שָּׁמַעְתְּ מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַפַּרְגּוֹד? אָמְרָה לָהּ: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁכָּל הַזּוֹרֵעַ בִּרְבִיעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה בָּרָד מַלְקֶה אוֹתוֹ. הָלַךְ הוּא וְזָרַע בִּרְבִיעָה שְׁנִיָּה. שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לָקָה, שֶׁלּוֹ — לֹא לָקָה.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this: «And» is it so that the dead do «not» know of the pain of others? «Wasn’t it taught» in a baraita: There was «an incident involving a pious man who gave a poor man a dinar on the eve of Rosh HaShana during drought years, and his wife mocked him» for giving so large a sum at so difficult a time? «And» in order to escape her incessant mockery, «he went and slept in the cemetery.» That night in his dream (Ritva, HaKotev, Maharsha), «he heard two spirits conversing with each other. One said to the other: My friend, let us roam the world and hear from behind the heavenly curtain [pargod],» which separates the Divine Presence from the world, «what calamity will befall the world. The other spirit said to her:» I «cannot» go with you, «as I am buried in a mat of reeds, but you go, and tell me what you hear. She went, and roamed, and came» back. «The other spirit said: My friend, what did you hear from behind the heavenly curtain? She replied: I heard that anyone who sows during the first rainy season» of this year, «hail» will fall and «strike his» crops. Hearing this, the pious man «went and sowed» his seeds «during the second rainy season.» Ultimately, the crops of «the entire world were stricken» by hail «and his» crops «were not stricken.»

segments.he: לַשָּׁנָה הָאַחֶרֶת הָלַךְ וְלָן בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, וְשָׁמַע אוֹתָן שְׁתֵּי רוּחוֹת שֶׁמְסַפְּרוֹת זוֹ עִם זוֹ. אָמְרָה חֲדָא לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ: בּוֹאִי וְנָשׁוּט בָּעוֹלָם וְנִשְׁמַע מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַפַּרְגּוֹד מַה פּוּרְעָנוּת בָּא לָעוֹלָם. אָמְרָה לָהּ: חֲבֶרְתִּי, לֹא כָּךְ אָמַרְתִּי לָךְ, אֵינִי יְכוֹלָה שֶׁאֲנִי קְבוּרָה בְּמַחְצֶלֶת שֶׁל קָנִים?! אֶלָּא לְכִי אַתְּ, וּמַה שֶּׁאַתְּ שׁוֹמַעַת בּוֹאִי וְאִמְרִי לִי. הָלְכָה וְשָׁטָה וּבָאָה. וְאָמְרָה לָהּ חֲבֶרְתָּהּ: חֲבֶרְתִּי, מַה שָּׁמַעְתְּ מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַפַּרְגּוֹד? אָמְרָה לָהּ: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁכָּל הַזּוֹרֵעַ בִּרְבִיעָה שְׁנִיָּה שִׁדָּפוֹן מַלְקֶה אוֹתוֹ. הָלַךְ וְזָרַע בִּרְבִיעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה, שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ נִשְׁדַּף וְשֶׁלּוֹ לֹא נִשְׁדַּף.
segments.en: «The following year,» on the eve of Rosh HaShana, the same pious man «went and slept in the cemetery» at his own initiative, and again «he heard the two spirits conversing with each other. One said to the other: Let us roam the world and hear from behind the heavenly curtain what calamity will befall the world. She said to her: My friend, have I not» already «told you» that «I cannot, as I am buried in a mat of reeds? Rather, you go, and tell me what you hear. She went, and roamed, and returned. The other» spirit «said to her: My friend, what did you hear from behind the curtain? She said to her: I heard that those who sow during the second rainy season blight will strike his» crops. That pious man «went and sowed during the first rainy season.» Since everyone else sowed during the second rainy season, ultimately, the crops «of the entire world were blighted and his» crops «were not blighted.»

segments.he: אָמְרָה לוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֶשְׁתָּקַד שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לָקָה וְשֶׁלְּךָ לֹא לָקָה, וְעַכְשָׁיו שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ נִשְׁדַּף וְשֶׁלְּךָ לֹא נִשְׁדַּף? סָח לָהּ כָּל הַדְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ. אָמְרוּ: לֹא הָיוּ יָמִים מוּעָטִים עַד שֶׁנָּפְלָה קְטָטָה בֵּין אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ חָסִיד וּבֵין אִמָּהּ שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ רִיבָה. אָמְרָה לָהּ: לְכִי וְאַרְאֵךְ בִּתֵּךְ שֶׁהִיא קְבוּרָה בְּמַחְצֶלֶת שֶׁל קָנִים.
segments.en: The pious man’s «wife said to him: Why is it that last year,» the crops «of the entire world were stricken and yours were not stricken, and now» this year, the crops «of the entire world were blighted and yours were not blighted? He related to her the entire story. They said: It was not» even «a few days» later that «a quarrel fell between the pious man’s wife and the mother of the young woman» who was buried there. The pious man’s wife «said to her» scornfully: «Go and I will show you your daughter,» and you will see that «she is buried in a mat of reeds.»

segments.he: לַשָּׁנָה הָאַחֶרֶת הָלַךְ וְלָן בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת וְשָׁמַע אוֹתָן רוּחוֹת שֶׁמְסַפְּרוֹת זוֹ עִם זוֹ. אָמְרָה לָהּ: חֲבֶרְתִּי, בּוֹאִי וְנָשׁוּט בָּעוֹלָם וְנִשְׁמַע מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַפַּרְגּוֹד מַה פּוּרְעָנוּת בָּא לָעוֹלָם. אָמְרָה לָהּ: חֲבֶרְתִּי, הֲנִיחִינִי, דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּינִי לְבֵינֵךְ כְּבָר נִשְׁמְעוּ בֵּין הַחַיִּים. אַלְמָא יָדְעִי.
segments.en: «The following year, he» again «went and slept in the cemetery, and heard the same spirits conversing with each other. One said» to the other: «My friend, let us roam the world and hear from behind the heavenly curtain what calamity will befall the world. She said to her: My friend, leave me» alone, as «words that» we have privately exchanged «between us have already been heard among the living. Apparently,» the dead «know» what transpires in this world.

segments.he: דִּילְמָא אִינִישׁ אַחֲרִינָא שָׁכֵיב, וְאָזֵיל וְאָמַר לְהוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: This is no proof; «perhaps another person,» who heard about the conversation of the spirits secondhand, «died and» he «went and told them» that they had been overheard.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: דִּזְעֵירִי הֲוָה מַפְקֵיד זוּזֵי גַּבֵּי אוּשְׁפִּיזְכָתֵיהּ. עַד דְּאָתֵי וְאָזֵיל לְבֵי רַב, שְׁכִיבָה. אֲזַל בָּתְרַהּ לַחֲצַר מָוֶת, אֲמַר לַהּ: זוּזֵי הֵיכָא? אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: זִיל שַׁקְלִינְהוּ מִתּוּתֵי צִנּוֹרָא דְּדָשָׁא בְּדוּךְ פְּלָן, וְאֵימָא לַהּ לְאִימָּא, תְּשַׁדַּר לִי מַסְרְקַאי וְגוּבְתַּאי דְּכוּחְלָא בַּהֲדֵי פְּלָנִיתָא דְּאָתְיָא לִמְחַר. אַלְמָא יָדְעִי!
segments.en: With regard to the deceased’s knowledge of what transpires, «come» and «hear» a proof, as it is told: «Ze’iri would deposit» his «dinars with his innkeeper. While he was going and coming to» and from «the school of Rav, she died,» and he did not know where she had put the money. «So he went after her to» her grave in «the cemetery and said to her: Where are the dinars? She replied: Go and get them from beneath the hinge of the door in such and such a place, and tell my mother» that «she should send me my comb and a tube of eyeshadow with such and such a woman who will» die «and come here tomorrow. Apparently,» the dead «know» what transpires in this world.

segments.he: דִּלְמָא דּוּמָה קָדֵים וּמַכְרֵיז לְהוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this proof: «Perhaps» the angel «Duma,» who oversees the dead, «comes beforehand and announces to them» that a particular individual will arrive the next day, but they themselves do not know.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: דַּאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הֲווֹ קָא מַפְקְדִי גַּבֵּיהּ זוּזֵי דְיַתְמֵי. כִּי נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ לָא הֲוָה שְׁמוּאֵל גַּבֵּיהּ. הֲווֹ קָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ: ״בַּר אָכֵיל זוּזֵי דְיַתְמֵי״. אֲזַל אַבָּתְרֵיהּ לַחֲצַר מָוֶת. אֲמַר לְהוּ: בָּעֵינָא אַבָּא! אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אַבָּא טוּבָא אִיכָּא הָכָא. אֲמַר לְהוּ: בָּעֵינָא אַבָּא בַּר אַבָּא. אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אַבָּא בַּר אַבָּא נָמֵי טוּבָא אִיכָּא הָכָא. אֲמַר לְהוּ: בָּעֵינָא אַבָּא בַּר אַבָּא אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הֵיכָא? אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ סְלֵיק לִמְתִיבְתָּא דִּרְקִיעָא. אַדְּהָכִי חַזְיֵיהּ לְלֵוִי דְּיָתֵיב אַבָּרַאי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַמַּאי יָתְבַתְּ אַבָּרַאי? מַאי טַעְמָא לָא סָלְקַתְּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ, דְאָמְרִי לִי: כָּל כִּי הָנָךְ שְׁנֵי דְּלָא סְלֵיקְתְּ לִמְתִיבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אַפָּס וְאַחְלֵישְׁתֵּיהּ לְדַעְתֵּיהּ, לָא מְעַיְּילִינַן לָךְ לִמְתִיבְתָּא דִרְקִיעָא.
segments.en: The Gemara cites another proof: «Come» and «hear,» as it is told: «They would deposit the money of orphans with Shmuel’s father» for safekeeping. «When Shmuel’s father died, Shmuel was not with him,» and did not learn from him the location of the money. Since he did not return it, Shmuel was called: «Son of» him who «consumes the money of orphans.» Shmuel «went after» his father «to the cemetery and said to» the dead: «I want Abba.» The dead «said to him: There are many Abbas here. He told them: I want Abba bar Abba. They said» to him: «There are also many people named Abba bar Abba here. He told them: I want Abba bar Abba, the father of Shmuel. Where» is he? «They replied: Ascend to the yeshiva on high. Meanwhile, he saw» his friend «Levi sitting outside» the yeshiva, away from the rest of the deceased. «He asked him: Why do you sit outside? Why did you not ascend» to the yeshiva? «He replied: Because they tell me» that for «all those years» that «you didn’t enter the yeshiva of Rabbi Afes, and» thereby «upset him, we will not grant you entry to the yeshiva on high.»

segments.he: אַדְּהָכִי וְהָכִי אֲתָא אֲבוּהּ, חַזְיֵיהּ דַּהֲוָה קָא בָכֵי וְאַחֵיךְ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא קָא בָכֵית? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּלַעֲגָל קָא אָתֵית. מַאי טַעְמָא אַחֵיכְתְּ? דַּחֲשִׁיבַתְּ בְּהַאי עָלְמָא טוּבָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי חֲשִׁיבְנָא — נְעַיְּילוּהּ לְלֵוִי. וְעַיְּילוּהוּ לְלֵוִי.
segments.en: «Meanwhile,» Shmuel’s «father came» and Shmuel «saw that he was crying and laughing.» Shmuel «said to» his father: «Why are you crying?» His father «replied:» Because «you will come here soon.» Shmuel continued and asked: «Why are you laughing?» His father replied: Because «you are extremely important in this world.» Shmuel «said to him: If I am important, then let them grant Levi entry» to the yeshiva. «And» so it was «that they granted Levi entry» to the yeshiva.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זוּזֵי דְיַתְמֵי הֵיכָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל שַׁקְלִינְהוּ בְּאַמְתָא דְרִחְיָא. עִילָּאֵי וְתַתָּאֵי — דִּידַן, וּמִיצְעֵי דְּיַתְמֵי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא עֲבַדְתְּ הָכִי? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי גָּנְבִי גַּנָּבֵי — מִגַּנְבוּ מִדִּידַן. אִי אָכְלָה אַרְעָא — אָכְלָה מִדִּידַן. אַלְמָא דְּיָדְעִי! — דִּילְמָא שָׁאנֵי שְׁמוּאֵל, כֵּיוָן דַּחֲשִׁיב קָדְמִי וּמַכְרְזִי: פַּנּוּ מָקוֹם.
segments.en: Shmuel «said to» his father: «Where is the orphans’ money? He said to him: Go» and «retrieve it from the millhouse,» where you will find «the uppermost and the lowermost» money «is ours, and» the money «in the middle» belongs to «the orphans.» Shmuel «said to him: Why did you do that? He replied: If thieves stole, they would steal from our» money on top, which the thief would see first. «If the earth swallowed up» any of it, it would swallow «from our» money, on the bottom. «Apparently,» the dead, in this case Shmuel’s father, «know» when others will die. Since Shmuel did not die the next day, clearly the angel Duma could not have informed them (Tosafot). The Gemara responds: «Perhaps Shmuel is different,» and «because he is so important they announce beforehand: Clear place» for his arrival.

segments.he: וְאַף רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן הֲדַר בֵּיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מִנַּיִן לַמֵּתִים שֶׁמְסַפְּרִים זֶה עִם זֶה — שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֵלָיו זֹאת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב לֵאמֹר״. מַאי ״לֵאמֹר״? — אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה: לֵךְ אֱמוֹר לָהֶם לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּעְתִּי לָכֶם כְּבָר קִייַּמְתִּיהָ לִבְנֵיכֶם.
segments.en: In any case, with regard to the crux of the issue, «Rabbi Yonatan also reconsidered» his opinion, «as Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said» that «Rabbi Yonatan said: From where» is it derived «that the dead converse with each other? As it is stated: “And the Lord said to him, this is the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying:» I will give it to your offspring” (Deuteronomy 34:4). «What is» the meaning of «“saying”?» It means that «God told Moses: Go and tell Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,» that «the oath that I swore to you I have already fulfilled for your descendants.»

segments.he: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּלָא יָדְעִי, כִּי אָמַר לְהוּ מַאי הָוֵי? אֶלָּא מַאי — דְּיָדְעִי? לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר לְהוּ?! לְאַחְזוֹקֵי לֵיהּ טֵיבוּתָא לְמֹשֶׁה.
segments.en: «And if it should enter your mind that» the dead «do not know, then what of it if he tells them?» The Gemara rejects this: «Rather what» will you say, «that» they «know?» Then «why does he» need «to tell them?» The Gemara replies: This is not difficult, as he is telling them so that «they will give credit to Moses.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר אַחֲרֵי הַמֵּת, כְּאִלּוּ מְסַפֵּר אַחֲרֵי הָאֶבֶן. אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי דְּלָא יָדְעִי, וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי דְּיָדְעִי וְלָא אִיכְפַּת לְהוּ.
segments.en: On this subject, «Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Anyone who speaks» negatively «after the deceased it is as if» he «speaks after the stone.» The Gemara offers two interpretations of this: «Some say» this is because the dead «do not know, and some say» that «they know,» but «they do not care» that they are spoken of in such a manner.

segments.he: אִינִי?! וְהָא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: חַד אִישְׁתַּעִי מִילְּתָא בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל וּנְפַל קַנְיָא מִטְּלָלָא וּבְזַעָא לְאַרְנְקָא דְמוֹחֵיהּ!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Is that so? Didn’t Rav Pappa say:» There was once «someone who spoke» disparagingly «after» the death of «Mar Shmuel and a reed fell from the ceiling, fracturing his skull?» Obviously, the dead care when people speak ill of them.

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי צוֹרְבָא מֵרַבָּנָן, דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תָּבַע בִּיקָרֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this: This is no proof that the dead care. Rather, a «Torah scholar is different, as God» Himself «demands» that «his honor» be upheld.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר אַחַר מִטָּתָן שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים נוֹפֵל בְּגֵיהִנָּם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהַמַּטִּים עֲקַלְקַלּוֹתָם יוֹלִיכֵם ה׳ אֶת פּוֹעֲלֵי הָאָוֶן שָׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל״. אֲפִילּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁשָּׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, ״יוֹלִיכֵם ה׳ אֶת פּוֹעֲלֵי הָאָוֶן״.
segments.en: Rabbi Yehoshua «ben Levi said» similarly: «One who speaks» disparagingly «after the biers of Torah scholars» and maligns them after their death will «fall in Gehenna, as it is stated: “But those who turn aside unto their crooked ways, the Lord will lead them away with the workers of iniquity; peace be upon Israel”» (Psalms 125:5). «Even» if he speaks ill of them «when there is peace upon Israel,» after death, when they are no longer able to fight those denouncing them (Tosafot); nevertheless «the Lord will lead them away with the workers of iniquity,» to Gehenna.

segments.he: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אִם רָאִיתָ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁעָבַר עֲבֵירָה בַּלַּיְלָה — אַל תְּהַרְהֵר אַחֲרָיו בַּיּוֹם, שֶׁמָּא עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה. ״שֶׁמָּא״ סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ? אֶלָּא וַדַּאי עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה. וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי — בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁבְּגוּפוֹ. אֲבָל בְּמָמוֹנָא — עַד דְּמַהְדַּר לְמָרֵיהּ.
segments.en: On a similar note, «it was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael: If you saw a» Torah «scholar transgress a prohibition at night, do not think» badly «of him during the day; perhaps he has repented» in the meantime. The Gemara challenges this: «Does it enter your mind» that only «perhaps» he has repented? Shouldn’t he be given the benefit of the doubt? «Rather, he has certainly repented.» The Gemara notes: «The idea» that one must always give a Torah scholar the benefit of the doubt and assume that he has repented refers specifically to «matters» affecting «himself, but,» if one witnesses a Torah scholar committing a transgression «involving the property» of another, one is not required to give him the benefit of the doubt. Rather, he should not assume that he has repented «until» he sees him «return» the money to «its owner.»

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה חד לחבריה: ידע אבון בהאי צערא?
moves.summary: One of R' Ḥiyya's sons, who have forgotten their learning, asks his brother whether their dead father knows of their distress.
moves.about: whether their dead father R' Ḥiyya knows of the anguish of his sons who have forgotten their learning

moves.cueHe: מנא ידע? והא כתיב
moves.summary: The brother denies the premise and brings Job 14:21 that the dead do not know.
moves.about: whether the dead know what happens to the living — the brother denies it and sets Job 14:21 against the question's premise

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה אידך: ולא ידע? והא כתיב
moves.summary: He counters with Job 14:22 and R' Yitzḥak's dictum, showing the dead have sensation.
moves.about: whether the dead know — Job 14:22 and R' Yitzḥak's dictum are set against Job 14:21 as cited by the brother

moves.cueHe: אמרי: בצערא דידהו — ידעי
moves.summary: The contradiction is resolved: the dead know their own pain but not the pain of others.
moves.about: reconciling the two Job verses by distinguishing knowledge of one's own pain from knowledge of another's

moves.cueHe: ולא? והתניא
moves.summary: A baraita is brought against the resolution: do the dead really not know the affairs of others?
moves.about: whether the dead know of the pain of others — the baraita's spirits know that their private words were repeated among the living, against the resolution that they know only their own pain

moves.cueHe: מעשה בחסיד אחד שנתן דינר לעני בערב ראש השנה
moves.summary: The baraita tells of a pious man who slept in a cemetery and overheard two spirits foretelling the year's calamity.
moves.about: bringing the baraita of the pious man and the two spirits

moves.cueHe: אמרה לו אשתו: מפני מה אשתקד של כל העולם כולו לקה
moves.summary: His wife learns the secret and taunts a bereaved mother with it, so the spirits' private words reach the living.
moves.about: he tells his wife the whole story of the spirits in the cemetery

moves.cueHe: אלמא ידעי
moves.summary: Since the spirit knows her words were repeated among the living, the dead evidently know.
moves.about: inferring from the spirit's complaint that her private words were repeated among the living that the dead know what happens in the world

moves.cueHe: דילמא איניש אחרינא שכיב
moves.summary: The proof is dissolved: perhaps someone who had heard died and brought the news.
moves.about: whether the baraita proves the dead know — perhaps another person died and brought them the news

moves.cueHe: תא שמע: דזעירי הוה מפקיד זוזי גבי אושפיזכתיה
moves.summary: A second proof: Ze'iri's dead innkeeper tells him where his money is and knows who will die tomorrow.
moves.about: Ze'iri used to deposit his money with his innkeeper, who died before he could recover it

moves.cueHe: אלמא ידעי
moves.summary: The dead evidently know what happens among the living.
moves.about: inferring from the innkeeper's knowledge that a particular woman will die tomorrow that the dead know what happens among the living

moves.cueHe: דלמא דומה קדים ומכריז להו
moves.summary: Rejected: perhaps the angel Duma announces arrivals to them in advance.
moves.about: whether the Ze'iri story proves the dead know — perhaps the angel Duma announces arrivals to them in advance

moves.cueHe: תא שמע: דאבוה דשמואל הוו קא מפקדי גביה זוזי דיתמי
moves.summary: A third proof: Shmuel goes to the cemetery to find his father and the orphans' money.
moves.about: orphans' money used to be deposited with Shmuel's father, and he died while Shmuel was away

moves.cueHe: אמאי יתבת אבראי? מאי טעמא לא סלקת?
moves.summary: Within the story, Shmuel asks Levi why he sits outside the heavenly academy; Levi answers that he had stayed away from R' Afes.
moves.about: where his father Abba bar Abba is to be found among the dead

moves.cueHe: אלמא דידעי
moves.summary: Since Shmuel's father knew his son would die soon, the dead evidently know.
moves.about: inferring from Shmuel's father knowing of Shmuel's coming death that the dead know what happens among the living

moves.cueHe: דילמא שאני שמואל
moves.summary: Rejected: Shmuel is exceptional, and an announcement is made in advance for one so eminent.
moves.about: whether the Shmuel story proves the dead know — perhaps Shmuel's eminence caused an advance announcement to be made for him

moves.cueHe: ואף רבי יונתן הדר ביה
moves.summary: R' Yonatan is reported to have retracted his earlier view that the dead do not know.
moves.about: R' Yonatan withdraws his earlier position that the dead do not know, a position stated outside this unit

moves.cueHe: מנין למתים שמספרים זה עם זה
moves.summary: He asks whence it is derived that the dead converse with each other.
moves.about: from where in Scripture it is derived that the dead converse with each other

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ״ויאמר ה׳ אליו זאת הארץ אשר נשבעתי לאברהם ליצחק וליעקב לאמר״
moves.summary: He answers from Deuteronomy 34:4, expounding ״לאמר״ as God's charge to Moses to tell the patriarchs.
moves.about: bringing Deuteronomy 34:4 as the source that the dead converse

moves.cueHe: ואי סלקא דעתך דלא ידעי, כי אמר להו מאי הוי?
moves.summary: If the dead do not know, telling them would be pointless — so the verse presupposes that they do.
moves.about: whether the dead know — if they do not, there would be no point in Moses telling them, so the verse implies they do

moves.cueHe: אלא מאי — דידעי? למה ליה למימר להו?!
moves.summary: But if they do know, the announcement is superfluous.
moves.about: whether the dead know — if they already know, Moses' announcement is superfluous

moves.cueHe: לאחזוקי ליה טיבותא למשה
moves.summary: Moses tells them so that they will credit him with the fulfilment of the oath.
moves.about: Moses tells the patriarchs even though they know, so that they will credit him with the fulfilment

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יצחק: כל המספר אחרי המת
moves.summary: R' Yitzḥak: speaking ill of the dead is like speaking to a stone.
moves.about: adducing R' Yitzḥak's dictum that speaking ill of the dead is like speaking to a stone

moves.cueHe: איכא דאמרי דלא ידעי, ואיכא דאמרי דידעי ולא איכפת להו
moves.summary: Two readings of his dictum: either the dead do not know, or they know and do not care.
moves.about: why speaking ill of the dead is futile — because they do not know, or because they know and do not care

moves.cueHe: איני?! והא אמר רב פפא
moves.summary: Rav Pappa's report — a reed split the skull of a man who disparaged Mar Shmuel — shows the dead do care.
moves.about: whether the dead are indifferent to being disparaged — the punishment of the man who spoke ill of Mar Shmuel shows they are not

moves.cueHe: שאני צורבא מרבנן
moves.summary: A Torah scholar is different: God Himself demands his honour, so the case proves nothing about the dead generally.
moves.about: the Mar Shmuel case proves nothing about the dead in general, since God Himself demands the honour of a Torah scholar

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי: כל המספר אחר מטתן של תלמידי חכמים
moves.summary: One who disparages dead Torah scholars falls into Gehenna, proven from Psalms 125:5.
moves.about: bringing Psalms 125:5 as the prooftext for the punishment of one who disparages dead Torah scholars

moves.cueHe: תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל: אם ראית תלמיד חכם שעבר עבירה בלילה
moves.summary: The school of R' Yishmael: do not suspect by day a scholar you saw transgress by night, for perhaps he repented.
moves.about: adducing the school of R' Yishmael's teaching that one must not suspect a Torah scholar the morning after seeing him transgress

moves.cueHe: ״שמא״ סלקא דעתך?
moves.summary: Only 'perhaps'? A scholar is owed more than that.
moves.about: whether a Torah scholar seen transgressing is only possibly repentant — שמא understates what he is owed

moves.cueHe: אלא ודאי עשה תשובה
moves.summary: Rather, he has certainly repented.
moves.about: the teaching must mean that the scholar has certainly repented, not merely that he may have

moves.cueHe: והני מילי — בדברים שבגופו, אבל בממונא
moves.summary: The presumption of repentance holds for bodily transgressions only; in money matters, not until he returns it.
moves.about: limiting the presumption of repentance to bodily transgressions, not to monetary ones, where it holds only once he returns the money

edges.about: whether their dead father R' Ḥiyya knows of the anguish of his sons who have forgotten their learning
bringing Job 14:21 as proof that the dead do not know
whether the dead know what happens to the living — the brother denies it and sets Job 14:21 against the question's premise
bringing Job 14:22 as proof that the dead do feel and therefore know
adducing R' Yitzḥak's dictum that maggots hurt the dead as a needle hurts living flesh, to show the dead have sensation
whether the dead know — Job 14:22 and R' Yitzḥak's dictum are set against Job 14:21 as cited by the brother
reconciling the two Job verses by distinguishing knowledge of one's own pain from knowledge of another's
bringing the baraita of the pious man and the two spirits
whether the dead know of the pain of others — the baraita's spirits know that their private words were repeated among the living, against the resolution that they know only their own pain
his wife provokes him for giving a whole dinar to a poor man in years of drought, driving him to sleep in the cemetery
edges.proposedPredicate: social.reproaches_conduct_of — «והקניטתו אשתו» — verbally reproves another's conduct as improper; rebuked is cued by נזף/שמתיה/לייט (formal censure) and said_to is bare non-dialectical speech

edges.cueHe: אמרה חדא לחברתה: חברתי, בואי ונשוט בעולם
edges.about: one spirit invites the other to roam the world and hear from behind the heavenly curtain what calamity is coming
edges.proposedPredicate: social.requests_of — «בואי ונשוט בעולם» — asks another party to do something with or for her, rather than asserting or asking a question

edges.cueHe: אמרה לה חברתה: איני יכולה, שאני קבורה במחצלת של קנים
edges.about: she cannot go out because she is buried in a mat of reeds, and asks her friend to go and report back

edges.cueHe: אמרה לה: שמעתי שכל הזורע ברביעה ראשונה ברד מלקה אותו
edges.about: reporting what she heard from behind the heavenly curtain about which sowing season will be struck

edges.cueHe: אמרה לו אשתו: מפני מה אשתקד של כל העולם כולו לקה ושלך לא לקה
edges.about: why his crops alone escaped the hail one year and the blight the next
he tells his wife the whole story of the spirits in the cemetery

edges.cueHe: אמרה לה: לכי ואראך בתך שהיא קבורה במחצלת של קנים
edges.about: in a quarrel she taunts the mother that her daughter is buried in a mat of reeds — the leak that reaches the dead
edges.proposedPredicate: social.reproaches_conduct_of — «לכי ואראך בתך» — a scornful taunt delivered to the other party's face in a quarrel; rebuked is formal censure (נזף/שמתיה) and said_to is bare non-dialectical speech
